title: Which leader owns a job's delivery?
body: Your question about B is answered above the questions, with a comparison of three options. Settled: Coordination owns your conversation and end-to-end delivery progress, and the map's Notes say it drives delivery. It does no substantive work itself. Engineering owns implementation, and Quality validates (round 1). Options: (A) The Engineering leader decides when the job branch is ready, hands validation to Quality, owns the PR and follows CI through to a tested PR. Coordination reports each step to you. A notes-only job is delivered by its own leader (Planning or Research). (B) Coordination owns delivery throughout. It decides, on Engineering's word, when the branch is ready for validation, receives Quality's verdicts and passes findings to Engineering, asks for the push, has the PR written by its own worker (pr moves to Coordination's worker list), and follows CI. (C) Split at Quality's pass. Engineering decides readiness and hands validation to Quality, and findings go straight between them. Once Quality passes, Engineering hands the job branch to Coordination, which asks for the push, has the PR written by its own worker (pr moves to Coordination's worker list), follows CI and reports to you. A red build goes back to Engineering. Notes-only jobs are delivered by Coordination too.
rec: C. It keeps the map's Notes (Coordination drives delivery) and makes everything you see come from the agent you talk to. It also keeps the technical fix loop direct between Engineering and Quality, which avoids B's main costs: an extra hop on every finding, and delivery traffic in your conversation's agent. A remains the cheapest in handoffs, if you prefer that.
options: A: Engineering owns delivery (notes-only jobs: the notes' own leader)
B: Coordination owns delivery throughout
C: split: Engineering and Quality until Quality passes, then Coordination

title: Who pushes the job branch to origin?
body: Settled: the job branch moves only when the daemon fast-forwards it to an accepted result, and only one party writes a branch at a time. Before every push, the job fetches its branch from origin and keeps any outside commits, never force-pushing over them (Define concurrent repository work and integration). The job branch's tip is always an accepted commit already on origin through its assignment branch, so nothing is lost while the job branch exists only in AsmAI's clone. Today agents perform every git and GitHub action themselves and record it as an effect (ADR 0002). Options: (A) The daemon pushes it when the delivery owner (R2-Q1) asks, with a plain push that is never forced. If origin has commits AsmAI did not make, the push is refused and recorded as an outside change, and a worker in Engineering merges them in, after which the push is retried. The daemon records the push as an effect. This makes the daemon the only party that ever moves the job branch, locally or on origin, and it is the daemon's first outward action. (B) A worker pushes it, inside a delivery assignment, from its workspace and records the effect, like any other git action.
rec: A. A worker pushing the job branch would be a second writer of the branch the daemon owns, and the push itself is mechanical: no judgement is needed once the delivery owner asks. Merging outside commits stays writing work for a worker either way.
options: A: the daemon, when the delivery owner asks; never forced
B: a worker in a delivery assignment

title: When is the job branch pushed and the PR opened?
body: Round 1 settled that a tested PR needs green CI on its exact head. Many repositories run CI only for pull requests, so a PR has to exist before that evidence can. Options: (A) Once, at delivery. When Quality passes the head, the job branch is pushed and the PR opened as a draft. When CI is green on that head, the PR is marked ready for review and Coordination reports it. If GitHub refuses a draft for that repository, the PR opens normally with '[not ready]' at the start of its title until then. A later change repeats the cycle on the same PR. (B) Early. The job branch is pushed after its first acceptance and after every later one, and a draft PR opens at the first push. It is marked ready when the tested-PR evidence is complete. (C) As A, but the PR opens ready for review straight away and is updated with the CI result.
rec: A. The PR appears once, when it is nearly ready, so the repository's watchers and CI see one delivery, not every acceptance. AsmAI's status line and asmai status already show progress before then. C would show a PR as ready for review before its CI has passed.
options: A: once, at delivery: pushed, draft PR, ready when CI is green
B: early: pushed after each acceptance, draft PR from the first push
C: as A, but opened ready for review straight away

title: Who writes the PR, and what goes in it?
body: Settled: evidence is summarized in the PR body, and no GitHub review is posted in your name (Q5). Agents use your gh credentials. The pr skill's template has Summary (the smallest view of the change), Evidence (before and after) and Merge Danger (one-way or two-way door, blast radius). Options: (A) A worker of the delivery owner (R2-Q1), in a short delivery assignment with the pr skill, writes the title and body, opens or updates the PR with gh, and records the effect. The body follows the repository's own PR template where it has one, and otherwise the pr skill's template. Either way it adds an AsmAI section covering the job and its mandate, the head commit Quality passed, the checks and CI results, advisory findings and gaps. It links the originating issue with 'Closes #n' only when the mandate is to resolve that issue, and with 'Refs #n' otherwise. The body is updated whenever the evidence changes. For a notes-only job, the body is a short 'notes only' summary. (B) The daemon fills a fixed AsmAI template from the journal, with no worker. (C) As A, but always the pr skill's template, ignoring repository templates.
rec: A. The Summary and Merge Danger sections need judgement about the change, which is worker work. Repository templates are repository instructions, which apply. 'Closes' only when the mandate says so keeps a merge from closing an issue that the job did not set out to resolve.
options: A: the delivery owner's worker with the pr skill; the repository's template, else the pr skill's; plus an AsmAI evidence section
B: the daemon fills a fixed template
C: as A, always the pr skill's template

title: Who waits for CI, and what happens when it fails?
body: CI often takes many minutes. Settled: workers whose dispatch is in progress count against the cap of 3 per provider (Define operating limits and visibility). Options: (A) The daemon watches the checks on the pushed head through gh, using no worker or allowance. When they are green, it marks the PR ready, records the delivery, and Coordination reports it. When they are red, the delivery owner (R2-Q1) receives the failing checks. It may re-run the failed jobs once if it judges the failure unrelated to the change, recorded as a delegated decision. Otherwise the fix goes to Engineering and then through Quality again. A newer push replaces the old wait. (B) A worker waits for CI inside a delivery assignment. (C) As A, but nothing is re-run: every failure gets a fix assignment.
rec: A. Waiting is not work and should not hold a slot under the cap. One recorded re-run covers flaky CI without hiding a real failure, because a second red result always gets a fix.
options: A: the daemon watches; red goes to the delivery owner, with one judged re-run allowed
B: a worker waits for CI
C: as A, never re-run

title: How does AsmAI know a repository has no CI?
body: Round 1 settled that a repository without CI says so, and the checks Quality ran then stand in. An empty list of checks can also mean CI is slow, broken or not yet triggered. no-mistakes refuses to treat an empty list as green without an explicit no-CI declaration. Options: (A) Per-repository configuration declares 'no CI'. Coordination's repository setup asks when a repository is added, and you can change it later. Otherwise AsmAI waits for at least one check on the head. If none appears within 15 minutes (a factory-wide setting), the job holds and you are asked whether the repository has CI. (B) No check within 15 minutes counts as no CI, and the PR states it as a gap.
rec: A. A broken CI trigger would otherwise turn into a quiet pass. The declaration is asked once per repository.
options: A: declared per repository; otherwise wait, then hold and ask me
B: no checks within 15 minutes means no CI

title: What if a repository's instructions name another way to push or open PRs?
body: For example, an AGENTS.md might say 'push through no-mistakes' or 'open PRs with scripts/release-pr'. Settled: repository instructions decide how work is done in a repository but never widen a mandate, and a conflict with the mandate is escalated (Define concurrent repository work and integration). AsmAI's own clone has only origin as a remote. Options: (A) AsmAI's delivery always pushes and opens the PR. Repository instructions shape what goes into the PR (templates, labels, checks to run) and Quality's Standards review, but never how the branch is pushed. An instruction that would hand the branch to another tool is listed as a gap in the PR body. (B) Each such instruction is escalated to you, per job. (C) AsmAI follows the repository's way of pushing.
rec: A. Pushing through another tool would put a second writer on the job branch, the reason no-mistakes was not adopted. Listing it as a gap lets you run that tool yourself on the delivered PR.
options: A: AsmAI's delivery always pushes; such an instruction is listed as a gap
B: escalate each one to me
C: follow the repository's way of pushing

title: Add these glossary terms?
body: Round 1 introduced three terms that later tickets and the specification will use. Proposed entries: Tested pull request: a job's pull request whose exact head commit has passed validation and the repository's CI, with its base taken in and its evidence and gaps stated. It is ready for the user to review and merge, and the factory never merges it. Avoid: ready PR, finished PR. Validation: Quality's independent check of a job branch at one exact commit, re-running the repository's checks and reviewing the change against the repository instructions and the job's mandate. Validation never changes the work. Avoid: QA, testing (when meaning Quality's check). Finding: a problem that validation reports. A blocking finding must be fixed before delivery. An advisory finding is reported, and no fix is required. A needs-you finding challenges the user's stated intent or a recorded decision, so it goes to the user. Avoid: issue, comment (when meaning a validation result). Options: (A) Add all three as written. (B) Add them with the changes in my notes. (C) Do not add them.
rec: A. Each is used precisely in this resolution and would otherwise be read loosely: 'tested', 'review' and 'issue' already mean other things.
options: A: add all three as written
B: add them with the changes in my notes
C: do not add them
